doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His marriage and daughters
summary: His wife of 56 years raised their two daughters, both with doctorates, while he traveled.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: You were traveling so much... I’d like to move onto a completely different tack. You were married for 56 years.
Right.
And you were traveling half the time.
Right.
It sounds like a very strong marriage.
Oh, yeah. My wife was from close to my hometown. I knew her many years before we got married. She saved every penny, heh-heh...
So you sent it home.
Oh, yeah. I sent money orders. Every week I’d send money orders. She raised the kids and put both of them through college. Both of them went on to get doctorates.
What are your kids’ names?
One of them, this one up here [POINTS TO PHOTOGRAPH BEHIND HIM] died. Lydia.
With the violin?
No, that’s Tracy. That’s my granddaughter. See, they moved...they changed the house around, so I don’t even know what’s up there any more.
How many kids did you have?
I had two.
Lydia was one.
And Carol.
They both got doctorates.
In what, if I may ask?
Carol’s is in psychology, and Lydia’s was in education. Some kind of... I don’t remember exactly what it was. In other words, she was a procurer for teachers down in Broward County.
Oh, in Florida.
Yes. She traveled all over the United States to the Black colleges, and tests the students and see if they were qualified to come back down there and teach.
Was your wife working during those years?
No.
